headings: Omnichannel Distribution and Customer Contact Center
paragraphs: In this Annual Report, unless otherwise indicated or the context otherwise requires, references to the "Company," "J.Jill," "we," "us," and "our" refer to J.Jill, Inc. and its consolidated subsidiaries. We operate on a 52- or 53-week fiscal year that ends on the Saturday that is closest to January 31. Each fiscal year generally is comprised of four 13-week fiscal quarters, although in the years with 53 weeks, the fourth quarter represents a 14-week period. References in this Annual Report to "Fiscal Year 2025" refer to the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, references to "Fiscal Year 2024" refer to the fiscal year ended February 1, 2025, and references to "Fiscal Year 2023" refer to the fiscal year ended February 3, 2024. Fiscal Years 2025 and 2024 are comprised of 52 weeks and Fiscal Year 2023 is comprised of 53 weeks.

J.Jill is a national lifestyle brand that provides apparel, footwear and accessories designed to help its customers move through a full life with ease. The brand represents an easy, thoughtful and inspired style that celebrates the totality of all women and designs its products with its core brand ethos in mind: keep it simple and make it matter. J.Jill offers a high touch customer experience through 256 stores nationwide and a robust ecommerce platform. J.Jill is headquartered outside Boston.

J.Jill has modernized its value proposition and introduced new customers to its relevant and compelling products through thoughtful, versatile designs that reflect the individuality of its customers. J.Jill has accomplished this by clearly communicating its offerings that align with its vision: to live in a world where the totality of every woman is seen, valued and celebrated. This permeates across all J.Jill touchpoints through authentic advertising, inclusive retail experiences and presentation of its offerings – whether the customer chooses to shop on the J.Jill website, in J.Jill retail stores, or through the J.Jill catalog.

J.Jill caters to a distinctive set of women – typically 45 years and older, college educated, and with an approximate median annual household income of $150,000. Her discretionary dollars are her own to spend and she leads a busy, yet balanced life and she is involved in her community. Her average tenure with the J.Jill brand is an industry-leading 10 plus years.

Additionally, as J.Jill retains her over time, she tends to migrate from being a single channel customer to a more valuable omnichannel customer. Omnichannel customers comprised approximately 24% of J.Jill's active customer base for Fiscal Year 2025, approximately 24% for Fiscal Year 2024, and approximately 23% for Fiscal Year 2023.

J.Jill's products are marketed under the J.Jill brand name and sold primarily through two channels: its ecommerce platform and catalog ("Direct") and its retail stores ("Retail"). J.Jill's thoughtful, versatile apparel, footwear and accessories reflect the individuality of each customer and are made to seamlessly take them through their day. J.Jill uses high quality fabrics and techniques for season-after-season comfort and style. J.Jill's products are available across the full range of sizes including Regular, Petite and Tall, and it provides one, size-integrated shopping destination for customers with sizes from Extra Small up to 2X in store and 4X online.

In addition to its core assortment, J.Jill has sub-brands. Each demonstrate a different design ethos and offers customers a mix of casual and refined apparel based on their needs. J.Jill offers versatile apparel that meets every moment of her life. Customers turn to J.Jill for work, travel, luxe loungewear, events and occasions, and premium casual clothing.
J.Jill also offers accessories to elevate the styling of our classic silhouettes including jewelry, bags, belts, shoes and scarves.

The J.Jill customer seeks newness and unique products. Through nine separate seasons, J.Jill flows designs and color palettes frequently – creating engagement and optionality for its customers. Substantially all of J.Jill's merchandise is designed in-house, creating newness through different fabrics, colors, patterns and silhouettes. J.Jill also utilizes the launch of its sub-brands, Pure Jill, Wearever, and Fit, to stagger new deliveries, and offers web edit capsules and omnichannel product refreshes to provide newness throughout each season. The close coordination between its teams ensures that its product and brand message is clearly communicated to its customers across all channels, bringing customers back regularly to see what's new.

J.Jill believes that its customers' purchasing decisions are influenced by the consistent experience it provides across its sales channels. For Fiscal Year 2025, J.Jill generated approximately 52% of total net sales through its Retail channel and approximately 48% of total net sales through its Direct channel. This balanced, omnichannel business model means J.Jill meets existing and prospective customers where and how they want to shop. Further, its robust customer database and analytical capabilities allow J.Jill to be focused and strategic in identifying high potential locations and optimizing its store footprint.

As of January 31, 2026, J.Jill operated 256 stores across 42 states with approximately half located in lifestyle centers and the remaining in premium malls; all J.Jill stores are leased. Its stores range in size from approximately 2,000 to 6,000 square feet, and the average store is approximately 3,700 square feet.

J.Jill's store designs showcase its brand, while elevating and simplifying the J.Jill shopping experience. Its stores provide a shared community of like-minded women and a welcoming, easy-to-shop environment with personalized attention. Its customer relies on trusted store associates to provide honest feedback and advice to help guide them. Through its concierge service, they can get early access to J.Jill's latest products or have its team pull items that complement their style and aesthetic. When the customer cannot find an item in-stock at their local store, J.Jill's in-store ordering platform ships available products to their home.

J.Jill believes its stores to be an important channel for its customers. J.Jill reviews and evaluates its store fleet and potential new store locations on various factors, including customer demographics within a market, concentration of existing customers, location of existing stores, center tenant quality and mix, rental economics and overall operating performance. J.Jill returned to net store growth in Fiscal Year 2024 and continued in 2025 with the addition of net four new stores. J.Jill will continue to review its fleet for optimization opportunities going forward, while also pursuing net new store openings.

headings: Risks Related to Our Business, Industry and Strategy

Our business is sensitive to macroeconomic conditions and we rely on consumer discretionary spending, which means we may be adversely affected by economic downturns and other macroeconomic conditions or trends.
Disruption in the economy may further affect our business, results of operations, liquidity, and financial results.
If we fail to acquire new customers in a cost-effective manner, it could have an adverse impact on our growth strategy as we may not be able to increase net revenue or profit per active customer.

Competitive pressures from other retailers as well as adverse structural developments in the retail sector may have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

Our business depends on effective marketing and increasing customer traffic and the success of our Direct channel depends on customers' use of our website and response to catalogs and digital marketing.

Reductions in the volume of mall traffic or the closing of shopping malls as a result of changing economic conditions or demographic patterns could significantly reduce our sales and leave us with unsold inventory.
The ability to accurately forecast our operating results and growth rate, which may adversely affect our reported results.
Inventory shrinkage could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

We occupy our stores under long-term leases, which are subject to future increases in occupancy costs, which we may be unable to renew on favorable terms and which may limit our flexibility to move to new locations.
Competitive pricing pressures with respect to shipping our merchandise to our customers may harm our business and results of operations.
The failure of our suppliers to comply with our social compliance program requirements could have a material adverse effect on our reputation, business, financial condition and results of operations.
Unseasonal or severe weather conditions may adversely affect our merchandise sales.

If our distribution and customer contact center is damaged or closed or if its operations are diminished, that could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We may face challenges managing rapidly advancing artificial intelligence in our business which could adversely affect our competitive position.
A delay in approving a budget and/or continuing appropriation legislation to fund the operations of the federal
Having a substantial amount of indebtedness under our Credit Agreements which matures in the near term, and the scheduled maturity dates are in close proximity to each other.
paragraphs: Investing in our common stock involves a high degree of risk. You should consider and carefully read all of the risks and uncertainties described below, as well as other information included in this Annual Report and in our other public filings. The risks described below are not the only ones facing us. The occurrence of any of the following risks or additional risks and uncertainties not presently known to us or that we currently believe to be immaterial could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition or results of operations. In such case, the trading price of our common stock could decline, and you may lose all or part of your original investment. This Annual Report also contains forward-looking statements and estimates that involve risks and uncertainties. Our actual results could differ materially from those anticipated in the forward-looking statements as a result of specific factors, including the risks and uncertainties described below.

Our business and operating results are subject to national and global economic conditions and their impact on consumer discretionary spending. Some of the factors that may negatively influence consumer spending include high levels of unemployment; higher consumer debt levels; reductions in net worth, declines in asset values, and related market and macroeconomic uncertainty; home foreclosures and reductions in home values; fluctuating interest rates, increased inflationary pressures and credit availability; rising fuel and other energy costs; rising commodity prices; and general uncertainty regarding the overall future political and economic environment. We have experienced many of these factors, including current inflationary pressures, and are experiencing negative impacts on client demand and discretionary spending as a result. Consumer purchases of discretionary items, including the merchandise that we offer, generally decline during recessionary periods or periods of economic uncertainty, when disposable income is reduced and when there is a reduction in consumer confidence. Furthermore, economic conditions in certain regions may also be affected by natural disasters, such as hurricanes, tropical storms, earthquakes, and wildfires; public health crises; and other major unforeseen events.

The current domestic and international political environment, including volatile trade relations, conflicts in multiple locations, and the related disruption to shipping lanes (for example, in the Middle East and surrounding areas) and civil unrest have resulted in uncertainty surrounding the future state of the global economy. There is uncertainty with respect to potential changes in trade regulations, sanctions and export controls, which increase volatility in the global economy and foreign currency exchange rates. This environment has affected and may continue to affect production and distribution lead times, increasing our costs and potentially affecting our ability to meet customer demand. If these disruptions persist, they may require us to modify our current sourcing practices, which may impact our product costs, and, if not mitigated, could have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations.

Additionally, other macroeconomic developments, such as efforts of governments to stimulate or stabilize the economy, international conflicts, trade disputes, sanctions, increased tariffs internationally, including between the United States and China and on imports into the United States from various countries may impact our business in an adverse manner, whether directly or indirectly, such as through their impacts on the financial positions and operations of our customers, suppliers, and other third parties with whom we do business.

Adverse macroeconomic changes could reduce consumer confidence and could thereby negatively affect our operating results. In challenging and uncertain economic environments, we cannot predict when macroeconomic uncertainty may arise, whether or when such circumstances may improve or worsen, or what impact such circumstances could have on our business. In recessionary periods and other periods where disposable income is adversely affected, we may have to increase the number of promotional sales or otherwise dispose of inventory for which we have already paid to manufacture, which could further adversely affect our profitability. It is difficult to predict when or for how long any of these conditions can affect our business and a prolonged economic downturn could have a material adverse effect on our business, financial condition and results of operations.

The extent to which economic disruptions caused by pandemics, epidemics, or public health emergencies will impact our business, liquidity, financial condition, cash flows and results of operations, depends on numerous evolving factors that we may not be able to accurately predict or assess. paragraphs: The following discussion and analysis should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and related notes thereto included elsewhere in this Annual Report. The following discussion contains forward-looking statements that reflect our plans, estimates and assumptions. Our actual results could differ materially from those discussed in the forward-looking statements. Factors that could cause such differences are discussed in the sections of this Annual Report titled "Risk Factors" and "Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements."

We operate on a 52 or 53-week fiscal year that ends on the Saturday that is closest to January 31. Each fiscal year is generally comprised of four 13-week fiscal quarters, although in the years with 53 weeks, the fourth quarter represents a 14-week period. References in this Annual Report to "Fiscal Year 2025" refer to the fiscal year ended January 31, 2026, references to the "Fiscal Year 2024" refer to the fiscal year ended February 1, 2025 and references to "Fiscal Year 2023" refer to the fiscal year ended February 3, 2024. Fiscal Years 2025 and 2024 are comprised of 52 weeks and Fiscal Year 2023 is comprised of 53 weeks.

The discussion that follows includes a comparison of our results of operations and liquidity and capital resources for Fiscal Years 2025 and 2024. For the discussion comparing the Fiscal Years 2024 and 2023, refer to Part II, Item 7. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations in our Fiscal Year 2024 Form 10-K, which was filed with the United States Securities and Exchange Commission on April 1, 2025.
All references in this Annual Report to "J.Jill", "we", "our", "us", "the Company" or similar terms are to J.Jill, Inc. and its subsidiaries.

J.Jill is a national lifestyle brand that provides apparel, footwear and accessories designed to help its customers move through a full life with ease. The brand represents an easy, thoughtful and inspired style that celebrates the totality of all women and designs its products with its core brand ethos in mind: keep it simple and make it matter. J.Jill offers a high touch customer experience through 256 stores nationwide and a robust ecommerce platform. J.Jill is headquartered outside Boston.

In assessing the performance of our business, we consider a variety of financial and operating metrics, including financial measures calculated in accordance with U.S. generally accepted accounting principles ("GAAP") and non-GAAP measures, such as:

Net sales consist primarily of revenues, net of merchandise returns and discounts, generated from the sale of apparel and accessory merchandise through our retail stores ("Retail") and through our website and catalog orders ("Direct"). Net sales also include shipping and handling fees collected from customers, and royalty revenues and marketing reimbursements related to our private label credit card agreement. Retail revenue is recognized at the time of sale or upon shipment if the sale is not immediately fulfilled, and Direct revenue is recognized upon shipment of merchandise to the customer.

Net sales are impacted by the size of our active customer base, product assortment and availability, marketing and promotional activities and the spending habits of our customers. Net sales are also impacted by the migration of single-channel customers to omnichannel customers who, on average, spend three times more than single-channel customers.

Total company comparable sales include sales net of returns from our retail stores that have been open for more than 52 weeks and from our Direct channel. This measure highlights the performance of existing stores open during the period, while excluding the impact of new store openings and closures. When a store in the total company comparable store base is temporarily closed for four or more days within a fiscal week, the store is excluded from the comparable store base; if it is temporarily closed for three or fewer days within a fiscal week, the store is included within the comparable store base. Certain of our competitors and other retailers may calculate total company comparable sales differently than we do. Our comparable sales are based on a 52-week period. The total company comparable sales calculation shifts the weeks in the fiscal year containing the fifty-third week to align like-for-like. As a result, the reporting of our total company comparable sales may not be comparable to sales data made available by other companies.

Number of stores reflects all stores open at the end of a reporting period. In connection with opening new stores, we incur pre-opening costs. Pre-opening costs include expenses incurred prior to opening a new store and primarily consist of payroll, travel, training, marketing, initial opening supplies and costs of transporting initial inventory and fixtures to retail stores, as well as occupancy costs incurred from the time of possession of a store site to the opening of that store. In connection with closing stores, we incur store-closing costs. Store-closing costs primarily consist of lease termination

penalties and costs of transporting inventory and fixtures to other store locations. These pre-opening and store-closing costs are included in selling, general and administrative expenses and are generally incurred and expensed within 30 days of opening a new store or closing a store.

Costs of goods sold ("COGS") consists of the direct costs of sold merchandise, which include customs, taxes, tariffs, duties, commissions and inbound shipping costs, inventory shrinkage, and adjustments and reserves for excess, aged and obsolete inventory. COGS does not include distribution center costs and allocations of indirect costs, such as occupancy, depreciation, amortization, or labor and benefits. We review our inventory levels on an ongoing basis to identify slow-moving merchandise and use markdowns to liquidate these products. Changes in the assortment of our products may also impact our gross profit. The timing and level of markdowns are driven by customer acceptance of our merchandise. The Company's COGS, and consequently gross profit, may not be comparable to those of other retailers, as inclusion of certain costs vary across the industry.

The variability in COGS is due to raw materials, transportation, freight costs, and tariffs. These costs fluctuate based on certain factors beyond our control, including labor conditions, inbound transportation or freight costs, energy prices, currency fluctuations and commodity prices. We place orders with merchandise suppliers in U.S. dollars and, as a result, are not exposed to significant foreign currency exchange risk.

Selling, general and administrative ("SG&A") expenses include all operating costs not included in COGS. These expenses consist primarily of all payroll and related expenses, occupancy costs, information systems costs and other operating expenses related to our stores and operations at our headquarters, including utilities, depreciation and amortization. These expenses also consist of marketing expense, including catalog production and mailing costs, warehousing, distribution and outbound shipping costs, customer service operations, consulting and software services, natural disaster related costs, professional services and other administrative costs. Additionally, our outbound shipping costs may fluctuate due to surcharges from shipping vendors based on demand for shipping services.

paragraphs: 本年度年報中，除非另有說明或語境另有要求，否則提及「本公司」、「J.Jill」、「我們」、「我們」及「我們的」均指 J.Jill, Inc. 以及其合併子公司。我們採用 52 或 53 週的財務年度，財務年度結束於距離 1 月 31 日最近的星期六。每個財務年度通常由四個 13 週財務季節組成，不過在有 53 週的年份，第四季則為 14 週。本年度年報中提及的「財務年度 2025」是指 2026 年 1 月 31 日結止的財務年度，提及的「財務年度 2024」是指 2025 年 2 月 1 日結止的財務年度，提及的「財務年度 2023」是指 2024 年 2 月 3 日結止的財務年度。財務年度 2025 和 2024 均為 52 週，財務年度 2023 則為 53 週。
J.Jill 是一個全國性的生活風格品牌，提供服飾、鞋類及配件，設計用以協助客戶輕鬆地經歷完整的人生。該品牌代表一種簡單、思緒周到且靈感來源的風格，慶祝所有女性的總體，並以其核心品牌理念設計產品：保持簡單，使其有意義。J.Jill 透過 256 家全美商店及強大的電商平台，提供高互動性的客戶體驗。J.Jill 的總部設於波士頓郊外。

J.Jill 已現代化其價值主張，並透過思緒周到且多用途的設計，將新客戶引入其相關且有吸引力的產品。J.Jill 已達成此目標，透過清楚傳達其與願景相符的產品：在一個每個女性的總體都被看見、被價值並被慶祝的世界中生活。此願景貫穿 J.Jill 的所有接觸點，透過真實的廣告、包容性的零售體驗及產品的呈現方式，無論客戶選擇在 J.Jill 網站購物、在 J.Jill 零售商店購物，或透過 J.Jill 目錄購物。
J.Jill 的目標客羣為一羣特殊的女性，通常為 45 歲以上，大學程度，且年家庭收入中位數約為 150,000 美元。她的閒錢是她自己可以支配的，她過著忙碌但平衡的生活，並參與社區活動。她與 J.Jill 品牌的平均合作年資為業界領先的 10 年以上。
此外，隨著 J.Jill 維持其客戶的時間增加，她傾向於從單一通路客戶轉變為更具價值的全通路客戶。全通路客戶在財務年度 2025 中約佔 J.Jill 活躍客戶羣的 24%，在財務年度 2024 中約佔 24%，在財務年度 2023 中約佔 23%。

J.Jill 的產品以 J.Jill 品牌名義行銷，並主要透過兩個通路銷售：其電商平台及目錄（「直接銷售」）以及其零售商店（「零售」）。J.Jill 的思緒周到且多用途的服飾、鞋類及配件反映每位客戶的個性，並設計成讓客戶順利度過一天。J.Jill 使用高品質的布料及技術，以實現季節後的舒適與時尚。J.Jill 的產品提供完整的尺碼範圍，包括標準、小號及高號，並為客戶提供一個整合的購物目的地，從極小號到 2X 在商店，4X 在線。
除了其核心產品系列，J.Jill 還擁有子品牌。每個子品牌展現不同的設計理念，並根據客戶需求提供混合的休閒與精緻服飾。J.Jill 提供多用途的服飾，以應對她生活的每一刻。客戶會選擇 J.Jill 來應對工作、旅行、奢華居家服、活動與場合，以及高檔休閒服飾。
J.Jill 還提供配件，以提升我們經典剪裁的時尚感，包括珠寶、包袋、腰帶、鞋子及圍巾。

J.Jill 的客戶追求新穎與獨特的產品。透過九個獨立的季節，J.Jill 不斷推出設計與色彩組合，創造與客戶的互動與選擇性。J.Jill 約百分之九十的商品為自行設計，透過不同布料、色彩、圖案與剪裁，創造新穎感。J.Jill 也會透過其子品牌 Pure Jill、Wearever 與 Fit 的發佈，來延長新產品的上架時程，並透過網路編輯小組與全通路產品更新，讓客戶在每個季節都能感受到新穎感。J.Jill 內部團隊的緊密協調，確保其產品與品牌訊息能清楚傳達給客戶，使客戶定期回訪以瞭解最新產品。
J.Jill 相信其客戶的購買決策受到其在各銷售通路提供一致體驗的影響。在財務年度 2025 年，J.Jill 約百分之五十二的總淨銷售額來自零售通路，約百分之四十八來自直營通路。這種平衡的全通路商業模式，使 J.Jill 能夠在客戶想要的時間與地點進行銷售。此外，其強大的客戶資料庫與分析能力，使 J.Jill 能夠聚焦且策略性地識別高潛力地點，並優化其門市據點。
截至 2026 年 1 月 31 日，J.Jill 在 42 個州運營 256 家門市，約一半位於生活風格中心，其餘則位於高檔購物中心；所有 J.Jill 門市皆為租賃。其門市大小約為 2,000 至 6,000 平方英呎，平均門市大小約為 3,700 平方英呎。

J.Jill 的門市設計展現其品牌，同時提升並簡化 J.Jill 的購物體驗。其門市提供一個志同道合女性的共鳴社羣，並營造一個歡迎、易於購物的環境，並提供個性化的服務。其客戶依賴受信任的門市員工提供誠實的意見與建議，以協助其做決策。透過其管家服務，客戶可獲得 J.Jill 最新產品的早期預覽，或讓其團隊協助尋找符合其風格與審美的商品。當客戶在當地門市找不到商品時，J.Jill 的門市訂購平台會將有庫存的商品送至其家中。
J.Jill 相信其門市是其客戶重要的購物通路。J.Jill 會根據多種因素評估其門市據點與潛在新門市地點，包括市場中的客戶人口統計、現有客戶集中度、現有門市位置、中心租戶品質與組合、租金經濟學與整體營運表現。J.Jill 在財務年度 2024 年恢復了淨門市成長，並在 2025 年持續增加，新增了淨四家新門市。J.Jill 將持續評估其門市據點以尋求優化機會，同時也將追求淨新增門市。

paragraphs: 下列討論與分析應與我們的合併財務報表及其相關附註一併閱讀，並包含於本年度報告的其他部分。下列討論包含前瞻性陳述，反映我們的計畫、預估與假設。我們的實際結果可能與前瞻性陳述中所討論的有所不同。導致這種差異的因素，已於本年度報告標題為「風險因素」與「前瞻性陳述警示」的節中討論。

我們採用52或53週的財務年度，財務年度結算日為距離1月31日最近的星期六。每一個財務年度通常由四個13週的財務季節組成，不過在有53週的年份中，第四季則為14週。本年度報告中提及的「財務年度2025」是指結算日為2026年1月31日的財務年度，提及的「財務年度2024」是指結算日為2025年2月1日的財務年度，提及的「財務年度2023」是指結算日為2024年2月3日的財務年度。財務年度2025與2024包含52週，財務年度2023包含53週。
下列討論包含對財務年度2025與2024的營運成果與流動性與資本資源的比較。有關財務年度2024與2023的比較，請參閱我們財務年度2024的Form 10-K中「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果的討論與分析」（Part II, Item 7）部分，該文件於2025年4月1日提交給美國證券交易委員會。
本年度報告中所有提及「J.Jill」、「我們」、「我們的」、「我們」、「本公司」或類似詞彙，均指J.Jill, Inc.及其子公司。
J.Jill為一間全國性的生活風格品牌，提供服飾、鞋類與配件，協助顧客輕鬆地經歷完整的人生。該品牌代表一種簡單、用心且靈感十足的風格，慶祝所有女性的總體，並以品牌核心價值觀為設計產品的考量：保持簡單，使其有意義。J.Jill透過256間全國性實體門市與強大的電商平台，提供高互動的顧客體驗。J.Jill總部設於波士頓附近。
在評估我們業務的表現時，我們考量多種財務與營運指標，包括根據美國通用會計準則（"GAAP"）計算的財務指標，以及非GAAP指標，例如：
淨銷售額主要由服飾與配件銷售產生的收入，扣除商品退貨與折扣後的金額，透過我們的零售門市（"零售"）與網站與目錄訂單（"直銷"）產生。淨銷售額也包含從顧客收取的運送與處理費用，以及與我們私標信用卡協議相關的 royalty 收入與行銷補償。零售收入在銷售時點或發貨時確認，若銷售無法立即履行則在發貨時確認，直銷收入在發貨至顧客時確認。
淨銷售額受我們活躍顧客數量、產品種類與可得性、行銷與促銷活動以及顧客的消費習慣影響。淨銷售額也受到單一通路顧客轉向全通路顧客的影響，平均而言，全通路顧客的消費金額為單一通路顧客的三倍。

總公司可比銷售額包含零售商店銷售額，扣除返還金額，這些商店營運超過52週，以及直接通路銷售額。此指標強調營運期間已營運的商店表現，同時排除新店開幕與關閉的影響。若總公司可比商店基礎中的商店在財務週內暫時關閉四天或以上，則該商店將被排除於可比商店基礎之外；若暫時關閉三天或以下，則該商店將包含於可比商店基礎內。部分競爭對手及其他零售商可能計算總公司可比銷售額的方式與我們不同。我們的可比銷售額基於52週期間。總公司可比銷售額計算會將財務年度內包含第五十三週的週數進行調整，以達到類似商品的對比。因此，我們的總公司可比銷售額報導可能與其他公司提供的銷售資料無法直接比較。

商店數量反映報告期間結束時所有營運中的商店數量。在開幕新店時，我們會產生開幕前成本。開幕前成本包含在開幕新店前產生的費用，主要為薪資、差旅、培訓、行銷、開幕初期用品及將初始存貨與展示架運送到零售商店的成本，以及從取得商店場地控制權至該商店開幕期間的佔用成本。在關閉商店時，我們會產生關閉商店成本。關閉商店成本主要為租賃終止罰款及將存貨與展示架運送到其他商店位置的成本。這些開幕前及關閉商店成本包含在銷售、一般及行政費用內，通常在開幕新店或關閉商店後30天內產生並費用化。

銷售成本（"COGS"）包含已售商品的直接成本，其中包括關稅、稅費、進口關稅、佣金及進口運輸費用、存貨減損，以及過多、陳舊及過時存貨的調整與備抵。銷售成本不包含配送中心費用及間接成本的分攤，例如租金、折舊、攤銷或勞動力及福利。本公司持續審查存貨水準，以識別銷售較慢的商品，並透過折扣處理這些商品。產品組合的變動也可能影響我們的毛利率。折扣處理的時機與程度取決於客戶對我們商品的接受度。本公司的銷售成本，以及因此產生的毛利率，可能與其他零售商不同，因為某些成本的包含方式會因產業而異。
銷售成本的變動係因原材料、運輸、運費及關稅所致。這些成本會根據某些超出本公司控制範圍的因素而波動，包括勞動條件、進口運輸或運費成本、能源價格、貨幣兌換率波動及商品價格。我們以美元向商品供應商下單，因此不會面臨顯著的外幣兌換風險。

銷售、一般及行政（"SG&A"）費用包含所有未包含在銷售成本中的營運成本。這些費用主要包含所有薪資及相關費用、租金成本、資訊系統成本及其他與我們門市及總部營運相關的營運費用，包括電力、折舊及攤銷。這些費用也包含行銷費用，包括目錄製作及寄送費用、倉儲、配送及出庫運輸費用、客戶服務營運、顧問及軟體服務、天然災害相關費用、專業服務及其他行政費用。此外，我們的出庫運輸費用可能因運輸供應商根據運輸服務需求而收取的附加費而波動。

本公司業務對總體經濟條件敏感，且我們依賴消費者非必要支出，這意味著我們可能因經濟衰退或其他總體經濟條件或趨勢而受到不利影響。
經濟動盪可能進一步影響本公司業務、營運結果、流動性及財務結果。
若我們無法以成本效益的方式取得新客戶，可能會對我們的成長策略產生不利影響，因為我們可能無法提高每活躍客戶的淨銷售額或利潤。
其他零售商的競爭壓力以及零售業的不利結構性發展，可能對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運結果產生重大不利影響。
本公司業務依賴有效的行銷及增加顧客人流量，而我們直銷通路的成功取決於顧客使用我們網站及對目錄及數位行銷的回應。
購物中心人流量減少或因經濟條件或人口結構變化而關閉購物中心，可能顯著降低我們的銷售額，並使我們面臨未售出存貨的問題。
準確預測本公司營運結果及成長率的能力，可能對我們的報告結果產生不利影響。
存貨減損可能對本公司之業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。
本公司租賃商店之租約為長期租約，未來租金成本可能上漲，本公司可能無法以有利條件續約，且可能限制本公司遷移至新址之靈活性。
針對將商品運送到客戶之運輸成本之競爭性價格壓力，可能對本公司之業務及營運成果造成損害。
若本公司之供應商未能遵守本公司之社會合規計畫要求，可能對本公司之聲譽、業務、財務狀況及營運成果造成重大不利影響。

paragraphs: 投資本公司的普通股涉及高度風險。您應考慮並仔細閱讀下列所描述的所有風險與不確定性，以及本年度報告及我們其他公開申報文件中包含的其他資訊。下列所描述的風險並非我們唯一面臨的風險。上述任何風險或目前未為我們所知或目前認為不重要的其他風險與不確定性發生，可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況或營運成果造成重大且不利的影響。在此情況下，本公司普通股的交易價格可能會下跌，您可能會喪失全部或部分原始投資。本年度報告亦包含涉及風險與不確定性的展望性陳述與預估。我們實際的結果可能與展望性陳述中預期的結果有重大差異，原因在於特定因素，包括下列所描述的風險與不確定性。

我們的業務與營運結果受國家與全球經濟條件及其對消費者非必要支出的影響。可能對消費者支出產生負面影響的因素包括失業率高、消費者負債水平高、淨財產減少、資產價值下跌，以及相關市場與總體經濟的不確定性、住宅 foreclosure 與住宅價值減少、利率波動、通貨膨脹壓力增加與信貸可得性、燃料及其他能源成本上升、商品價格上升，以及對總體未來政治與經濟環境的普遍不確定性。我們已經驗過許多這些因素，包括目前的通貨膨脹壓力，並因此經驗到客戶需求與非必要支出的負面影響。在經濟衰退期或經濟不確定期，消費者對非必要商品的購買，包括我們所提供的商品，通常會減少，當可支配所得減少且消費者信心下降時。此外，某些地區的經濟狀況也可能受自然災害，如颶風、熱帶氣旋、地震與野火、公共衛生危機及其他重大未預見事件的影響。

目前國內與國際的政治環境，包括貿易關係的波動、多個地區的衝突，以及對航運通道（例如中東及周邊地區）與民事動亂所造成的幹擾，導致對全球經濟未來狀態的不確定性。對於潛在的貿易規則變更、制裁與出口管制的不確定性，會增加全球經濟與外幣匯率的波動性。此環境已影響並可能繼續影響生產與配送的交貨時間，增加我們的成本，並可能影響我們滿足客戶需求的能力。如果這些幹擾持續存在，我們可能需要修改目前的來源策略，這可能會影響我們的產品成本，若無法緩解，可能會對我們的業務與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
此外，其他總體經濟發展，例如政府刺激或穩定經濟的措施、國際衝突、貿易爭議、制裁、國際間的關稅增加，包括美國與中國之間的關稅，以及從各國進口至美國的關稅，可能會以直接或間接的方式對我們的業務產生不利影響。

不利的總體經濟變動可能會降低消費者信心，進而對我們的營運結果產生負面影響。在困難與不確定的經濟環境中，我們無法預測總體經濟不確定性何時會出現，是否或何時會改善或惡化，以及這些情況對我們業務可能產生的影響。在經濟衰退期或其他可支配所得受到不利影響的時期，我們可能必須增加促銷銷售的數量，或以其他方式處置我們已支付製造費用的存貨，這可能會進一步對我們的利潤率產生不利影響。預測這些條件何時或持續多久會影響我們的業務，是非常困難的，而長期的經濟衰退可能會對我們的業務、財務狀況與營運成果造成重大不利影響。
疫情、流行病或公共衛生緊急事件所造成的經濟動盪對我們的業務、流動性、財務狀況、現金流與營運成果的影響程度，取決於許多不斷演變的因素，而我們可能無法準確預測或評估這些因素。這些因素包括，但不僅限於，疫情、流行病或公共衛生緊急事件的持續時間與範圍；對經濟的負面影響；對零售需求與消費者信心的短期與長期影響；我們成功應對這些影響的能力，包括潛在
